title: Compact Integration Accelerator Playset (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working draft of a compact, reproducible integration accelerator for new internal teams and small customers. The goal is to get a developer from 0 -> embedded demo in a 90 minute lab: install, wire the SDK, basic telemetry, and one simple production guardrail (circuit breaker + fallback to a smaller model).

Scope and constraints
- Focus: hosted API + local dev loop (no Dedicated/Private deploy plumbing).
- Assumes engineer has mac/linux laptop, Docker, node 18+ or Python 3.10+.
- Minimal infra: uses lightweight sample backend (Express/FastAPI) and a tiny front-end demo (static HTML + fetch).
- Telemetry: wire in a pre-made telemetry probe (prometheus-lite + local trace & event collector).

High-level timeline (90-minute lab)
- 0–10m: onboarding + goals + quick environment checks
  - Verify: node/pip, docker, git, API key in env (REDWOOD_API_KEY).
  - Quick checklist provided to participant at start.
- 10–30m: SDK install + quick hello-world call (sync + streaming example)
  - Command copy/paste and explanation of token billing.
- 30–55m: integrate SDK into sample backend, add retry/circuit-breaker policy
  - Inject a simple fallback (model-variant or cached reply) for latency > 500ms.
- 55–75m: add telemetry and smoke tests (latency, error-rate thresholds)
  - Run a small traffic generator, watch dashboard, identify a regression.
- 75–90m: wrap up, checkpoints, next steps for production readiness

Minimal commands for participants (copy/paste friendly)
- Clone starter repo:
  git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-accelerator-starters.git starter && cd starter/compact-playset
- Install (node):
  npm ci && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_XXXXXXXX
- Run backend (dev):
  npm run dev:backend
- Run frontend: open ./frontend/index.html in browser or run static server:
  npx serve frontend -p 4000
- Smoke example (curl):
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"summarize: Redwood inference"}' | jq .

Playset components and files
- /backend: Express + SDK wiring, middleware for telemetry events, retry wrapper.
- /frontend: minimal UI for chat/generation, demonstrates streaming chunk handling.
- /telemetry: small docker-compose with prom-lite + jaeger-mini + grafana-lite dashboards.
- /tests: k6 scripts for load smoke, small regression prompt set.

Key implementation patterns (why these choices)
- Continuous batching emulation: show how SDK batcher can reduce per-token cost; include toggle to turn batching on/off for demo.
- KV cache demo: illustrate prefix caching to speed repeated queries.
- Circuit breaker and fallback: practical guardrail that links to Redwood routing policy — explained as a pattern for production.

Guided instructor notes (for 1 mentor + up to 8 participants)
- Pre-lab: create a workspace in Google Drive with starter keys and invite participants.
- Walk the group through env checks and commands. Keep the first 10 minutes high-level.
- When integrating SDK, pause to explain cost telemetry (token breakdown) in the Console.
- For the telemetry section, intentionally introduce a regression (increase latency) and let participants triage using the provided dashboards.

Common friction points & mitigation tips
- Missing API key: supply temporary class keys and a helper script that validates key permissions.
- Local Docker networking edge-cases: provide a troubleshooting doc with common port conflicts and overrides.
- Slow streaming behavior in certain browsers: recommend Chrome + show a terminal-based streaming tester.

Unresolved questions (needs engineering/product alignment)
- Which default model should we recommend for a low-cost starter? (open: tiny-1.0 vs base-2.7)
- Should the lab include a one-click provisioner for ephemeral Demo Projects in Hosted API? (LR-198)
- Telemetry retention for demo projects: how long should probe data persist in shared environments?

Action items (owners & near-term milestones)
- Jordan Kim: produce final lab README and instructor script (ETA: 2025-02-20)
- Marcus Li: add batching toggle and KV cache sample (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/724) (ETA: 2025-02-14)
- Aisha Patel: build demo telemetry dashboard template and Grafana JSON (ETA: 2025-02-18)
- Samira Gomez: craft customer-facing 1-pager that maps lab outcomes to product value (ETA: 2025-02-25)

Metrics for success (how we will judge the playset)
- Time-to-first-generation < 20 minutes for 80% of participants.
- Post-lab survey: >90% of participants say they can integrate the SDK into a prototype.
- 25% of lab participants convert to a follow-up Dedicated evaluation within 60 days.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting snippets
- Validate API key scope:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami
- Local trace viewer (open): http://localhost:16686
- Re-run smoke with batching off:
  export REDWOOD_BATCHING=off && npm run smoke

Notes to self
- Keep language light and avoid deep infra-dive; the goal is confidence, not completeness.
- Collect the 10 most common participant questions during first two runs and fold into FAQ.

End of draft.
